title: No. It is only a word, and a barrier stands behind them.
subtitle: The request refused, then the Barzakh
then: Ibn Kathir says kalla is {trap}a word of rebuke: We will not accept it{/trap}. His request is {trap}just talk, not accompanied by action{/trap}. Then comes the Barzakh, which Mujahid called {idea}a barrier between this world and the Hereafter{/idea}, lasting until the Day of Resurrection.
now: "I'll start next Monday." "After Ramadan." "When the kids are older." {trap}Those are words.{/trap} {idea}The verse says words without deeds are what the dying man offers, and they are refused.{/idea}
old: My good intentions count, even if I have not acted yet.
new: An intention only becomes real when I act on it, while I still can.
try: Turn one "I will someday" into something you do before tonight.

title: When the Horn is blown, family ties will not help.
subtitle: No lineage, no asking after each other
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}lineage will be of no avail; a father will not ask about his son{/trap}, even if he sees him. Ibn Masud said a voice will call: {idea}whoever is owed something, come and take it{/idea}, and a person will be glad to be owed even a little by his father, child or spouse.
now: "Do you know who my family is?" Or the quiet comfort that your parents are pious, so you will be fine. {idea}On that Day, your own record walks with you.{/idea} So does every small wrong you owe your family.
old: My family's goodness will cover for me.
new: I will stand on my own deeds, so I settle what I owe people now.
try: Settle one small thing you owe a family member today: money, an apology, a promise.

title: Heavy scales mean success.
subtitle: Even one extra good deed can tip it
then: Ibn Abbas said this is {reward}the one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds, even by one{/reward}. They are the ones who {reward}attained what they wanted and were saved{/reward}. The surah that opened with "the believers have succeeded" returns to the same word.
now: Smiling at the tired cashier. Picking up the litter outside the masjid. Texting your mum good night. {idea}You will never know which small deed tipped your scale.{/idea}
old: Small good deeds do not really count.
new: Any good deed could be the one that makes my scale heavy.
try: Do three tiny good deeds today and do not tell anyone.

title: Light scales mean losing your own self.
subtitle: The worst loss is the loss of the soul
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}when evil deeds outweigh good deeds{/trap}; they are doomed and {trap}have ended up with the worst deal{/trap}. Not a lost fortune but {trap}a lost self.{/trap}
now: You panic over a lost wallet, a failed investment, a broken phone screen. {idea}Those losses can be replaced. This verse names the one loss that cannot.{/idea} And today you can still add to the other side.
old: The worst thing that could happen is losing what I have.
new: The worst loss is losing myself, and I can work against it today.
try: Ask Allah tonight to make your scale heavy, and do one good deed to start.

title: The Fire meets the faces that turned away.
subtitle: A sober warning, told to protect you

row.title: to turn you while you can

then: Ibn Kathir links this to verses saying {trap}fire will cover their faces{/trap} and they will not be able to ward it off. Ibn Abbas explained their look as {trap}frowning{/trap}. It describes the end of those whose scales were light.
now: Your face turned toward the screen at prayer time. Your face turned away from the person asking for help. {idea}The warning is about your face, and today you choose where it turns.{/idea}
old: Warnings about Hell are only meant to scare people.
new: The warning is a mercy telling me to turn my face toward Allah now.
try: At your next prayer, place your forehead down slowly and ask Allah to protect your face from the Fire.

title: Were My verses not recited to you?
subtitle: No excuse left after the message came
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells them: {idea}I sent Messengers, revealed Books, and cleared the confusion, so you have no excuse.{/idea} He cites: We never punish until We have sent a Messenger.
now: You have a Quran app on your phone. Translations in your language. Lectures for free. {idea}The verse you are reading right now has been recited to you.{/idea}
old: I did not know enough to be responsible.
new: The message has reached me, and that is both a gift and a responsibility.
try: Read the meaning of one more verse today, slowly, as if it was sent to you.

title: Our wretchedness overcame us, they will say.
subtitle: A confession that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}evidence was established against us, but we were so doomed we could not follow it, so we went astray.{/trap} They admit everything, but only after the door has closed.
now: You know the habit that keeps beating you. You could say it to Allah today: {idea}my Lord, my weakness wins sometimes, help me.{/idea} The same confession, said now, is the start of change.
old: I will admit my faults when I have to.
new: Confessing my faults to Allah today is a mercy, not a defeat.
try: Tell Allah honestly today one weakness that keeps beating you, and ask for help.

title: Take us out, and if we return, we are wrongdoers.
subtitle: A promise made from the wrong side of the door
then: They will ask: {trap}our Lord, bring us out, and if we go back to what we did, we will be wrongdoers.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to another verse: {trap}is there any way to get out?{/trap} There is none, because they associated partners while the believers worshipped Him alone.
now: After the hangover, the fight, the lost money, you swear: never again. {idea}You get to make that promise now, in this world, where it can still be kept.{/idea}
old: I will change once things get bad enough.
new: The time to promise and keep it is now, while I still have the world.
try: Make one sincere "never again" today about a habit, and take one step to keep it.

title: Stay in it, despised, and do not speak to Me.
subtitle: The door of asking finally closes
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}do not ask for this again, for I will not respond{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said these are the words of Ar-Rahman when silencing them. It is the most sober moment in the surah: {trap}asking itself is no longer accepted.{/trap}
now: Today Allah says: call on Me, I will answer. {reward}You can speak to Him at 3 a.m., in traffic, in a whisper.{/reward} The verse shows what it means to lose that, so you treasure it now.
old: I can always talk to Allah later.
new: Being allowed to speak to Allah is a gift I should use every day.
try: Talk to Allah for five minutes today in your own words, about anything.

title: A group of My servants said: forgive us, have mercy.
subtitle: The dua of the ones who were mocked
then: Allah reminds the people of the Fire of {idea}a party of My servants{/idea} who used to pray: {reward}our Lord, we believe, so forgive us and have mercy on us, You are the best of the merciful.{/reward} Ibn Kathir calls them His believing servants and close friends.
now: Your coworker who steps out to pray. Your quiet aunt who whispers dua all through the family dinner. {idea}Allah calls such people "My servants".{/idea} You can be one of them with one sincere sentence.
old: Only very pious people are Allah's special servants.
new: Those who humbly ask for forgiveness are the ones Allah calls His own.
try: Memorize this dua today: Rabbana amanna faghfir lana warhamna wa anta khayrur-rahimin.

title: You mocked them until it made you forget Me.
subtitle: How ridicule hardens the mocker
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}you made fun of them for calling on Me and praying to Me{/trap}, and {trap}your hatred for them made you forget what I would do to you{/trap}. He cites: the criminals used to laugh at the believers and wink at each other.
now: The group chat sends a meme about the "too religious" friend. Everyone laughs, including you. {trap}Mocking someone's worship slowly dulls your own.{/trap}
old: It is just a joke; it does not hurt anyone.
new: Mocking someone's sincerity can make me forget Allah myself.
try: If anyone jokes about someone's worship today, do not join. Change the subject kindly.

title: Their patience was rewarded; they are the winners.
subtitle: The mocked become the successful
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}for the harm and mockery you inflicted on them, I have caused them to attain the victory of joy, safety, Paradise and salvation from the Fire.{/reward} {idea}Patience was what turned the mockery into reward.{/idea}
now: You wear your hijab to a new job and catch the looks. You leave the party early to pray and hear the comments. {idea}Every bit of patience is being written down.{/idea}
old: Putting up with ridicule for my faith is a loss.
new: Patience with mockery is exactly what Allah rewards.
try: The next time someone teases your faith, answer calmly, then say alhamdulillah to yourself.
